justification.reason: Three uninterrupted arms under the same protocol and the same non-resume execution code already differ at update 2, in every final parameter hash and in every final logits receipt. Exact cross-process hash or logits equality is therefore not a valid restore criterion; the measured uninterrupted spread is the only observed noise envelope.
justification.conclusion: Every A/B scalar difference is smaller than the corresponding A/A pairwise maximum. Exact hashes and logits differ in A/A as well.

rule.within_envelope: absolute A/B delta is less than or equal to the largest pairwise absolute A/A delta for the same step and metric
rule.zero_envelope: if the A/A envelope is zero, the A/B delta must be exactly zero
rule.reference: the uninterrupted arm from the same comparison run as the resumed arm; not an arbitrary other arm
mandatory_exact_conditions: update 1 loss and gradient norm are exactly equal across all arms
the first/resume boundary fingerprint is exactly equal when both arms emit it
the resumed checkpoint receipt, model-start hashes and data/schedule cursor validate
applies_to: aggregate parameter, gradient and optimizer-moment norm summaries
per-tensor parameter, buffer and moment norm summaries when instrumented

effect.note: The policy can qualify a future bounded resource/numerical experiment, but it cannot turn a historical exact failure into a pass.
